text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

text: RESULTS: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with a possible pneumonia. No pleural effusion noted.

speaker: Doctor

That confirms a lung infection; have you been experiencing any fever, chills, or night sweats alongside this? Additionally, do you have any history of heart disease or recent travel?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC), Blood_Culture, and Sputum_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work is reassuring, but the chest X-ray clearly shows a pneumonia in your right lower lobe. Has your cough been productive with yellow or green mucus, or is it dry and hacking? Are you currently able to eat and drink without difficulty, or are you feeling too weak?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has mostly been dry, though I do cough up some white sputum occasionally. I am still able to eat and drink normally, though I do feel quite short of breath when I try to walk a bit. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Lower Lobe Pneumonia (likely atypical or early bacterial given the consolidation but normal initial blood work).
